chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Fadhl, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the cow that is sacrificed for Udhiyah; he said: 'It suffices for seven people.'

key_terms.الْبَقَرَةِ: The cow (specifically in the context of sacrifice)
key_terms.يُضَحَّى بِهَا: Sacrificed for Udhiyah (the ritual sacrifice during Hajj)

ai.seo_question: How many people can share in the sacrifice of one cow during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a single cow suffices for seven individuals, aligning with the general principle for Udhiyah where larger animals accommodate more participants. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing the specific capacity of cattle compared to sheep, which typically serve only one person, thereby facilitating communal participation in the Hajj sacrifice.
